skill.name: uspto-database
skill.description: Search USPTO patent and trademark records, retrieve prosecution histories, assignments, citations, and status data, and support prior-art and portfolio analysis.
skill.summary: Search and analyze public USPTO patent and trademark data through documented APIs and included Python clients.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The skill performs expected outbound HTTPS requests to documented USPTO and PatentsView services using a user-provided API key. No embedded credentials, shell execution, reconnaissance, or prompt injection were found. The trademark CLI can expose an API key through command history or process listings.

remediation.issue: The trademark CLI accepts an API key through --api-key, which can expose the secret to shell history and process listings.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the command-line key option and require USPTO_API_KEY or a protected credential file with restrictive permissions.

remediation.issue: The included HTTP clients do not set request timeouts or implement retry and backoff behavior.
remediation.suggestion: Set explicit connection and read timeouts, then retry transient failures and rate-limit responses with bounded exponential backoff.

content.value_statement: Patent and trademark research often requires several USPTO services and query formats. This skill provides documented workflows and Python clients for unified IP research.
actual_capabilities: Searches patents by keyword, inventor, assignee, CPC classification, patent number, or date range.
Retrieves patent details, citations, assignees, inventors, and selected text fields from PatentSearch.
Retrieves trademark status, goods and services, owner details, and prosecution history through TSDR.
Summarizes PEDS examination timelines, transaction histories, office actions, and current application status.
Provides assignment, citation, litigation, PTAB, and office-action integration examples.
limitations: Requires a user-supplied USPTO API key and network access for PatentSearch, TSDR, and assignment endpoints.
PatentSearch documentation states coverage through June 30, 2025; service availability and coverage can change.
Included clients do not implement caching, retries, backoff, or request timeouts.
Results are research aids and are not legal opinions or complete clearance searches.

use_cases.title: Screen Technical Prior Art
use_cases.description: Find patents by technical terms, classifications, assignees, and dates before deeper claim review.

use_cases.title: Review Prosecution History
use_cases.description: Summarize application status, transaction events, office actions, pendency, and allowance history.

use_cases.title: Monitor Trademark Portfolios
use_cases.description: Check registration status, ownership, goods and services, and prosecution events across selected marks.

prompt_templates.title: Look Up a Patent
prompt_templates.prompt: Find patent [PATENT NUMBER]. Summarize its title, grant date, inventors, assignee, abstract, classifications, and available citations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner lookup for one known patent number.

prompt_templates.title: Search a Technology Area
prompt_templates.prompt: Search patents for [KEYWORDS] from [START DATE] to [END DATE]. Group results by assignee and CPC subclass, then identify relevant records.
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused discovery using terms and dates.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Trademark Portfolio
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these trademark serial numbers: [NUMBERS]. Report current status, owner, goods and services, recent prosecution events, and records needing attention.
prompt_templates.scenario: Portfolio review for several known marks.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Combined IP Analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [PATENT OR COMPANY] across PatentSearch, PEDS, assignments, citations, litigation, and PTAB records. Separate verified facts, missing data, and research gaps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced research across multiple USPTO data sources.

output_examples.input: Find patents about battery thermal management granted during 2024.
output_examples.output: A ranked table listing patent number, title, grant date, assignee, inventors, abstract relevance, and CPC subclass, followed by stated search limits.
A concise status brief covering the mark, filing date, registration details, owner information, goods and services, and recent prosecution events.

output_examples.input: Summarize the prosecution history for application 16123456.
output_examples.output: A dated timeline of transaction codes, office actions, responses, current status, pendency, and any missing records requiring direct verification.

best_practices: Keep API keys in protected environment variables and never include them in prompts, logs, or repositories.
Narrow searches with dates, classifications, and selected fields to reduce response size and rate-limit pressure.
Verify time-sensitive status, ownership, and legal conclusions against current official USPTO records.
anti_patterns: Do not paste real API keys into examples, command arguments, prompts, or saved transcripts.
Do not treat keyword matches or automated status labels as legal conclusions.
Do not run large portfolio queries without pagination, caching, rate controls, and failure handling.

faq.question: Does this skill require a USPTO API key?
faq.answer: Yes. PatentSearch, TSDR, and assignment requests require a user-provided USPTO API key.

faq.question: Can it search patents by inventor or company?
faq.answer: Yes. The patent client supports inventor, assignee, keyword, CPC classification, patent number, and date-range searches.

faq.question: Can it retrieve patent examination history?
faq.answer: Yes. The PEDS helper retrieves application data, transactions, office actions, status summaries, and prosecution metrics when records are available.

faq.question: Can it monitor trademark status?
faq.answer: Yes. The trademark client retrieves status, goods and services, owner data, prosecution history, and basic attention flags.

faq.question: Does it provide legal advice or clearance opinions?
faq.answer: No. It organizes public data for research, but a qualified professional must evaluate legal significance and completeness.

faq.question: How should I protect my API key?
faq.answer: Use USPTO_API_KEY in a protected environment. Avoid command-line arguments, prompts, logs, and committed configuration files.
